'''''Hitman''''' is a 2016 [[stealth video game]] developed by [[IO Interactive]] and published by [[Square Enix]]. The game, which has six episodes, is the sixth mainline entry in the [[Hitman (franchise)|''Hitman'' franchise]], the first installment of the ''World of Assassination'' trilogy, and the successor to ''[[Hitman: Absolution]]'' (2012). The [[Single-player video game|single-player]] story follows [[Genetic engineering|genetically engineered]] assassin [[Agent 47]] as he goes on a worldwide adventure and solves a mysterious series of seemingly unconnected assassinations. ''Hitman'' features a number of large, open-ended [[Sandbox game|sandboxes]] that Agent 47 can freely explore. The game presents the player with various assassination opportunities, many of which are unconventional. IO Interactive introduced a "live component" to the game with new content being regularly delivered in downloadable form.

Each episode is set in a location: [[Paris]], [[Sapienza (Hitman)|Sapienza]], [[Marrakesh]], [[Bangkok]], [[Colorado]] and [[Hokkaido (Hitman)|Hokkaido]]. [[Square Enix Europe]] set up [[Square Enix Montréal|a Montréal studio]] to work on the next ''Hitman'' game, but IO Interactive returned to lead the game's development following the under-performance of ''Absolution''. The title was conceived as a reimagining of the franchise as the team attempted to integrate the gameplay of ''Absolution'' with the open-endedness of earlier installments of the series. According to the team, ''Hitman'' is a puzzle game with action and stealth elements; the developers refined the [[simulation]] and [[artificial intelligence]] of each level. The game adopted an episodic model and the team envisioned the [[Games as a service|game as a service]]. It was marketed as a "World of Assassination" and provided a platform that would expand and evolve over time, and inspire a trilogy of games.

''Hitman'' was released episodically for [[PlayStation 4]], [[Windows]], and [[Xbox One]] from March to October 2016. Upon release, it received positive reviews; critics praised the game's episodic release format, locations, level design, and its replayability but criticised the always-online requirement and excessive handholding. The game underperformed commercially and caused publisher [[Square Enix]] to divest from IO Interactive in May 2017. Following a [[management buyout]], IO retained the rights to the series and partnered with [[Warner Bros. Interactive Entertainment]] to produce a sequel titled ''[[Hitman 2 (2018 video game)|Hitman 2]]'', which was released in November 2018. The ''World of Assassination'' trilogy concluded with ''[[Hitman 3]]'', released in January 2021. In January 2023, ''Hitman'' was delisted from sales after IO Interactive rebranded ''Hitman 3'' as ''Hitman: World of Assassination'',{{efn|The ''World of Assassination'' branding was originally used for the Stadia release of ''Hitman 2'', and later ''Hitman 3''.}} with the contents of the previous two ''Hitman'' games becoming available to ''Hitman 3'' owners, free of charge.

== Gameplay ==
[[File:Hitman gameplay screenshot.jpg|left|thumb|In this gameplay screenshot, [[Agent 47]] is disguised as a [[fashion model]] in the Paris map.|alt=A screenshot of the game, showing Agent 47 disguised as a fashion model, walking down a catwalk surrounded by an audience]]

''Hitman'' is a [[stealth video game]] in which players control a genetically enhanced assassin called [[Agent 47]] from a [[third-person perspective]] as he carries out assassinations of various targets across the globe.<ref name="redesigning 47"/> As in other games in the [[Hitman (franchise)|''Hitman'' series]], players have a large amount of freedom in their approach to their assassinations.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.vg247.com/2015/06/16/hitman-e3-2015-pc-ps4-xbox-one/|title=E3 2015: Hitman invites players to step into a live world of assassination|first=Stephany|last=Nunneley|work=[[VG247]]|date=15 June 2015|access-date=15 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303195838/http://www.vg247.com/2015/06/16/hitman-e3-2015-pc-ps4-xbox-one/|archive-date=3 March 2016|url-status=live}}</ref> Players may use weapons including explosives,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/hitman-rubber-duck-challenge/|title=Pushing the boundaries of common sense reveals Hitman's true depth. Time for the rubber duck challenge|first=Martin|last=Kitts|work=[[GamesRadar]]|date=18 April 2020|access-date=16 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190720123645/https://www.gamesradar.com/hitman-rubber-duck-challenge/|archive-date=20 July 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> pistols,<ref name="PolyGuide"/> assault rifles,<ref name="the verge"/> and long-range sniper rifles;<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usgamer.net/articles/hitman-elusive-target-how-to-kill-the-congressman|title=Hitman: Elusive Target - How to Kill The Congressman|first=Bill|last=Lavoy|work=[[USgamer]]|date=27 May 2018|access-date=16 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180204200332/http://www.usgamer.net/articles/hitman-elusive-target-how-to-kill-the-congressman|archive-date=4 February 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> they may also assassinate the target at close range using bladed weapons or throwable items.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2017/jan/31/hitman-review-a-beautiful-puzzle-box-of-a-game|title=Hitman review – a beautiful puzzle box of a game|first=Jack|last=De Quidt|work=[[The Guardian]]|date=31 January 2017|access-date=16 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191008135842/https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2017/jan/31/hitman-review-a-beautiful-puzzle-box-of-a-game|archive-date=8 October 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>

Agent 47 is vulnerable in a firefight; thus, eliminating targets silently is preferred. He can use his specially equipped [[garrote]] wire to strangle his victims<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.wired.com/2016/03/hitman-review/|title=Hitman Is a Thrilling Return, But You Can't Play It All at Once|magazine=[[Wired (magazine)|Wired]]|first=Daniel|last=Starkey|date=14 March 2016|access-date=16 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200311184121/https://www.wired.com/2016/03/hitman-review/|archive-date=11 March 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> or disguise his killings as accidental deaths, such as poisoning the target's food<ref name="PolyGuide"/> or drowning them in a toilet.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.polygon.com/e3-2014/2015/6/16/8790429/the-new-hitman-begins-dec-8-with-a-digital-release|title=The new Hitman begins 8 Dec with a digital release|first=Owen S.|last=Good|work=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]|date=16 June 2015|access-date=21 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150618181839/http://www.polygon.com/e3-2014/2015/6/16/8790429/the-new-hitman-begins-dec-8-with-a-digital-release|archive-date=18 June 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> The game also includes scripted opportunities that require the completion of multiple tasks. A player's mission performance review is rated with a five-star rating system and is influenced by factors such as time elapsed, the number of non-target NPCs killed, sightings of 47 performing illegal activities, appearances on [[CCTV camera]]s, and discoveries of victims' bodies.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.polygon.com/2016/3/22/11286282/hitman-mission-ratings-explained|title=Hitman mission ratings, explained|work=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]|date=22 March 2016|access-date=16 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170430140750/http://www.polygon.com/2016/3/22/11286282/hitman-mission-ratings-explained|archive-date=30 April 2017|url-status=live}}</ref>

IO Interactive introduced a "live component" to ''Hitman''; new content, which was regularly delivered in downloadable form, includes time-limited missions called "Elusive Targets". If a player fails to kill an elusive target before the mission expires, or alerts targets and allows them to escape, the targets will not return. Players are rewarded for successful killings with cosmetic rewards. Unlike the main game, players cannot save their games when they are completing the Elusive Target missions.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/hitmans-real-time-live-content-explained-detailed/1100-6434918/|title=Hitman's Real-Time "Live Content" Explained, Detailed|first=Eddie|last=Makuch|work=[[GameSpot]]|date=18 February 2016|access-date=16 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160717041815/http://www.gamespot.com/articles/hitmans-real-time-live-content-explained-detailed/1100-6434918/|archive-date=17 July 2016|url-status=live}}</ref> "Escalation Contracts", which are contracts created by the developers, include stages that require players to complete tasks such as assassinating a target using a specific weapon or disguise. By completing a stage, players progress through the escalation and the level of difficulty will increase with new challenges to comply with or changes to the level.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/how-hitman-online-modes-work/|title=IO explains how Hitman's constantly-shifting online challenges change the game|first=Sam|last=Prell|work=[[GamesRadar]]|date=19 February 2016|access-date=16 April 2020|archive-date=30 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200330164759/https://www.gamesradar.com/how-hitman-online-modes-work/|url-status=live}}</ref> ''Hitman: Absolution''{{'}}s Online Contracts mode also returns in ''Hitman'',<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.polygon.com/2016/3/22/11285820/hitman-features-contracts-guide-explained|title=Hitman's features, challenges, contracts and live events, explained|work=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]|date=22 March 2016|access-date=30 August 2020|archive-date=17 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170417224121/http://www.polygon.com/2016/3/22/11285820/hitman-features-contracts-guide-explained|url-status=live}}</ref> allowing players to assign up to five NPCs as assassination targets, set requirements for their killings, and share their contracts with and compete with other players.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2016-03-11-hitman-2016-guide-4044?page=4|title=Hitman (2016) - How to create and execute interesting Contracts|first=Stace|last=Harman|work=[[Eurogamer]]|date=11 March 2016|access-date=16 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180203021506/http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2016-03-11-hitman-2016-guide-4044?page=4|archive-date=3 February 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Synopsis ==
In 1999, an unnamed man is initiated into the International Contract Agency (ICA) and demonstrates exceptional aptitude as an assassin. The ICA is unable to verify his background or uncover any information about him, which disturbs Erich Soders, the ICA's training director. With the help of his handler, Diana Burnwood, the initiate passes a final test that Soders had rigged against him. The director reluctantly approves the initiate for field duty and washes his hands of the matter. The man tells Diana to call him [[Agent 47|"47"]] and leaves to await further instructions; this prologue leads into the events of ''[[Hitman: Codename 47|Codename 47]]'', the first game in the series.

Twenty years later, 47 completes a series of contracts provided by Diana, who has risen to a senior position in the ICA. At first, the contracts appear to be unrelated, but Diana gradually uncovers information that an unknown individual referred to as the "Shadow Client" has covertly coordinated these contracts to attack a secretive organization called "Providence", whose existence and total control over global affairs were thought to be a myth. The Shadow Client uses the ICA and 47 to kill Providence agents, making the ICA appear culpable and hiding his own involvement. The game ends with Diana being approached by a representative of Providence, who requests that the ICA deal with the Shadow Client.

=== Plot ===
The Shadow Client performs an assassination for Viktor Novikov, a fashion mogul and head of the international spy ring IAGO, and receives a copy of all of IAGO's files as payment. Using the files to identify Providence's secret operations, the Client sends an anonymous warning to [[MI6]] of an impending IAGO auction of a stolen [[non-official cover]] (NOC) list that will take place at a [[Paris]] [[fashion show]] by Novikov's label, Sanguine. As a result, MI6 hires 47 to prevent the sale; he assassinates Novikov and his business partner, IAGO's true leader, Dalia Margolis, at the fashion show.

The Client sets two more ICA contracts in motion to disrupt Providence's activities without exposing himself. He first discloses a secret project to develop a deadly [[Ethnic bioweapon|weaponized virus]] to a disgruntled shareholder in the Ether Biotech Corporation, knowing that the shareholder will then hire 47 to assassinate Silvio Caruso and Francesca De Santis, the scientists in charge of the project, and destroy the virus prototype housed at Caruso's private lab in the fictitious Italian town of [[Sapienza (Hitman)|Sapienza]]. Providence dispatches an agent to investigate the incident; the Client ambushes and kills him, and takes a key in his possession.

The second contract involves the Client disclosing an impending military [[coup d'état|coup]] in Morocco to Hamilton-Lowe, an international contractor with lucrative Moroccan government contracts. The company hires 47 to eliminate General Reza Zaydan, the mastermind of the coup, and fugitive bank CEO Claus Hugo Strandberg—both of whom are undercover Providence operatives—in [[Marrakesh]]. As 47 completes the contract, the Client breaches a Providence vault in [[New York City]] and steals valuable information on Providence's assets and operatives. The leaders of Providence realize that a coordinated attack has been launched against them.

The Client puts a third ICA contract in motion to reveal another Providence member, the reclusive media tycoon Thomas Cross. Cross had ordered a coverup that enabled his son, famed [[indie rock]] singer Jordan Cross, to escape legal consequences for the murder of his girlfriend Hannah Highmoore by disguising her death as an apparent accident; the Client reveals the truth to her family. The Highmoores hire 47 to kill Jordan Cross and Ken Morgan, the Cross family lawyer and fellow Providence member who oversaw the coverup, while both are staying at a private resort in [[Bangkok]]. Deploying forces from a [[Private army|private militia]] under his control, the Client kidnaps Thomas Cross from Jordan's funeral and kills him, then steals billions of dollars from his offshore bank accounts. The ICA, realizing an unknown party has benefited from the Cross contract, re-examines 47's previous contracts and discovers the Client's role in setting them up.

The ICA learns of a training camp for the Client's militia, based in an old industrial farm in rural [[Colorado]]. Seeking to eliminate the Client for his manipulation, the agency orders a premature operation due to the intervention of Soders, a member of ICA's executive board. 47 is sent to the camp to eliminate the militia's leader, [[Eco-terrorism|eco-terrorist]] Sean Rose and three other key militia members. 47 discovers a secret room filled with the Client's research, revealing both the connections of the previous contracts to Providence and the Client's obsession with 47 himself. Diana also discovers that Soders is a mole for Providence and has been manipulating the agency on their behalf. The Client, who has been secretly tracking 47, uses this opportunity to go into hiding.

47 assassinates Soders and his Providence liaison, [[yakuza]] associate and fixer Yuki Yamazaki, at a hospital in [[Hokkaido]], where Soders is set to receive needed medical treatment in exchange for a list of all active ICA operatives. Subsequently, Providence uncovers the Client's role in the attacks. An unnamed Providence member approaches Diana on a train, seeking to hire the ICA to target the Client. Diana refuses but starts to reconsider when the Providence member offers to reveal information about 47's past.

=== ''The Sarajevo Six'' ===
In this alternative storyline, 47 receives contracts to assassinate the six former members of Sigma, a [[Plausible deniability|deniable operations]] [[paramilitary]] unit of the [[private military company|private military contractor]] Cicada, who committed war crimes during the [[siege of Sarajevo]] but evaded prosecution by the [[International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia]]. 47 tracks each Sigma member—starting with the group's former commander and working his way down—to all six of the main mission settings, with the events and characters of each location serving as backdrops. As the missions progress, security increases and the targets become more paranoid and cautious, increasing the difficulty.

For the final contract, 47 is sent to a hospital in Hokkaido to both eliminate the final Sigma member, Taheiji Koyama, and retrieve files documenting the unit's operations from the hospital's records. If 47 chooses to approach the target, Koyama will reveal that he financed the contracts, wanting to get justice for Sigma's victims. Now that he is dying from a terminal illness, Koyama instructs 47 to publicize the files after killing him. 47 honors Koyama's request, but both he and Diana conclude that public indifference will likely relegate Sigma's atrocities to obscurity.

=== ''Patient Zero'' ===
A [[doomsday cult]] that masquerades as a self-help group, named "Liberation", is using an upcoming exhibition at a luxury resort in Bangkok to provide cover for a [[Biological agent|bio-weapon]] attack. 47 receives a contract from a mysterious billionaire using the alias "Locksley" to eliminate the cult's leader Oybek Nabazov and his second-in-command, Sister Yulduz. As 47 makes his escape, Diana notices a series of digital messages being transmitted from the resort's network, which are revealed to be [[Dead man's switch|signals]] meant to activate the cult's [[sleeper agent]]s worldwide as a contingency once Nabazov's death is confirmed.

The ICA identifies two sleeper agents, Brother Akram and celebrity author Craig Black, who are meeting at a private event in Sapienza to exchange a weapon identical to the one in Bangkok, which 47 retrieves after eliminating the targets. ICA intel then confirms the origin of another signal, which leads to a mercenary camp in Colorado where Dr. Bradley Paine, a [[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention|CDC]] specialist and secret cult member, has already begun infecting personnel. Forced to maintain his distance to prevent infection, 47 assassinates Paine with a sniper rifle, along with four victims of the Nabazov virus.

Diana's analysts intercept a memo, indicating Japanese authorities have recently detained a man on a flight to Australia who showed signs of infection, and have ordered him to be quarantined at a hospital in Hokkaido. 47 infiltrates the hospital to eliminate the man, who is identified as Owen Cage, a radical virus researcher who helped design the Nabazov virus and infected himself with the intention of becoming [[Index case|patient zero]]. An additional target is Klaus Liebleid, an Ether scientist overseeing the quarantine effort while secretly trying to extract as much information about the virus as he can, so that Ether can [[Reverse engineering|reverse engineer]] Cage's work and profit from it. Despite Cage being kept in isolation, the virus can spread to other people and 47 must kill all infected individuals, if such a scenario arises, to eliminate the virus. During the debriefing, 47 and Diana note that the entire plot was beyond the scope of a cult, implying that Liberation was backed by a higher power. With the contract closed, the two move onto other targets.

== Development ==

=== Origin ===
Danish company [[IO Interactive]] developed all of the mainline ''[[Hitman (franchise)|Hitman]]'' games. Prior to the launch of ''[[Hitman: Absolution]]'' (2012), publisher and IO's owner [[Square Enix]] announced it had established a new studio named [[Square Enix Montréal]] to work on future ''Hitman'' games.<ref>{{cite web |last=Lund |first=Karsten |date=25 October 2012 |url=http://gamasutra.com/blogs/KarstenLund/20121025/179479/The_Future_Hitman_Game_on_a_Postit_Square_Enix_Montral.php |title=The Future Hitman Game, on a Post-it: Square Enix Montréal |publisher=[[Gamasutra]] |access-date=11 August 2013 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130811215230/http://gamasutra.com/blogs/KarstenLund/20121025/179479/The_Future_Hitman_Game_on_a_Postit_Square_Enix_Montral.php |archive-date=11 August 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Due to cutbacks and layoffs at IO Interactive, other projects were stopped and the company started working on a new ''Hitman'' game,<ref>{{cite web |last=Cowan |first=Danny |date=17 June 2013 |url=http://www.joystiq.com/2013/06/17/report-io-interactive-cancels-projects-loses-half-of-staff-to/ |title=Report: IO Interactive cancels projects, loses half of staff to layoffs |publisher=[[Joystiq]] |access-date=11 August 2013 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130811215608/http://www.joystiq.com/2013/06/17/report-io-interactive-cancels-projects-loses-half-of-staff-to/ |archive-date=11 August 2013 |url-status=live }}</ref> and Square Enix Montréal focused on developing smartphone and tablet versions of ''Hitman'' and other games.<ref>{{cite web |last=Usher |first=Anthony |date=21 June 2013 |url=http://www.pocketgamer.co.uk/r/iPhone/Hitman/news.asp?c=51832 |title=Square Enix Montréal working on smartphone and tablet versions of Hitman and 'other brands' |publisher=[[Pocket Gamer]] |access-date=11 August 2013 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130811220116/http://www.pocketgamer.co.uk/r/iPhone/Hitman/news.asp?c=51832 |archive-date=11 August 2013 |url-status=live }}</ref> Most of the members of the development team at IO Interactive only worked on ''Absolution'', not older games of the series, such as ''[[Hitman: Blood Money]]'' (2006).<ref name="Hitman Rise and fall">{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_stW6JvB4SI&t=210s|title=The Fall & Rise of Hitman (Documentary)|first=Danny|last=O'Dwyer|work=[[Noclip]]|via=[[YouTube]]|date=29 July 2019|access-date=7 June 2020|archive-date=6 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210206053324/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_stW6JvB4SI&t=210s|url-status=live}}</ref> 

''Absolution'' was controversial for removing many of the franchise's traditional gameplay elements and being linear rather than the large, open sandbox levels of the older games, despite being more accessible. When the team brainstormed ideas for the next entry in the franchise, they strove to integrate the gameplay of ''Absolution'' and the open levels of ''Blood Money''. According to Christian Elverdem, this goal was "daunting" during the early stage of the game's development because they needed to upgrade their in-house Glacier [[game engine]] to accommodate these larger maps and most of the team did not have experience building sandboxes.<ref name="Hitman Rise and fall"/> According to Michael Vogt, the game's lead writer, the title was designed to be a "soft reboot" and a "reimagining" of the franchise.<ref name="redesigning 47"/> After nearly four years of development, production concluded with a total cost of over $70 million.<ref> {{cite podcast| url= https://gamemakersnotebook.libsyn.com/exploring-the-world-of-hitman-with-io-interactives-hakan-abrak| title= Exploring the World of Hitman with IO Interactive's Hakan Abrak| website= Interactive.org| publisher= Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences Foundation| host= Orth, Adam| date= 19 December 2024| time= 49:51| access-date=26 February 2025}}</ref>

=== Design ===
The major story beats and the destinations were decided by a small group of development leads, after which a team would be responsible for each level's design, rules, targets, and other details to create a self-contained game world.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sQ0LlNfr8ZI&t=1315s|title=Revealing the Tricks Behind Hitman's Level Design|first=Danny|last=O'Dwyer|work=[[Noclip]]|via=[[YouTube]]|date=5 August 2019|access-date=7 June 2020|archive-date=3 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211203141031/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sQ0LlNfr8ZI&t=1315s|url-status=live}}</ref> The first level the team created, Paris, was the [[vertical slice]] for the game; it set the gameplay rules, general level design, and the number of [[non-playable character]]s for future episodes. According to Elverdem, every level is "fully simulated" and the player is free to explore and observe the behaviours of the AI.<ref name="simulation"/> If the player eliminates a certain NPC, the simulation adjusts itself and continues to function, though it will also react to players' actions.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2015/08/07/gamescom-2015-hitman-brings-back-the-best-of-blood-money|title=Gamescom 2015: Hitman Brings Back the Best of Blood Money|first=Luke|last=Reilly|work=[[IGN]]|date=16 July 2015|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170508064409/http://www.ign.com/articles/2015/08/07/gamescom-2015-hitman-brings-back-the-best-of-blood-money|archive-date=8 May 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> The team listened to feedback from [[Playtesting|playtester]]s and adjusted the game accordingly. For instance, after some playtesters complained about the level being too punitive, the team introduced the concept of escorting, in which NPCs escort Agent 47 back to a public space if he is found trespassing, whereas in the early version, the guards would attack Agent 47.<ref name="simulation">{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EjvrTa6IKW8|title=How the Simulation of a Hitman Level Works|first=Danny|last=O'Dwyer|work=[[Noclip]]|via=[[YouTube]]|date=31 July 2019|access-date=7 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200529052044/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EjvrTa6IKW8|archive-date=29 May 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[File:Amalfi sea view Italy.JPG|thumb|right|[[Amalfi]] in [[Italy]] inspired the design and the aesthetic of "[[Sapienza (Hitman)|Sapienza]]", the second episode.|alt=A 2006 photograph of Amalfi from off the coast]]

The team perceived ''Hitman'' as a [[Puzzle video game|puzzle game]] with action and [[stealth game|stealth]] elements; they had several major design concepts.<ref name="simulation"/> The first concept was named "Swiss cheese"; according to the team, the term means players would be presented with an ample options, and there were multiple ways to move in and out of a level.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/stayingin/tech-gaming/hitman-2016-developer-interview-how-iointeractive-s-reboot-was-inspired-by-swiss-cheese-a3124071.html|title=Hitman 2016 developer interview: how Io-Interactive's reboot was inspired by Swiss cheese|first=Talal|last=Musa|work=[[Evening Standard]]|date=26 November 2020|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160320131011/http://www.standard.co.uk/stayingin/tech-gaming/hitman-2016-developer-interview-how-iointeractive-s-reboot-was-inspired-by-swiss-cheese-a3124071.html|archive-date=20 March 2016|url-status=live}}</ref> Regardless of how the player chooses to infiltrate a place, the team made sure that there are no "visual dead ends", and that players will eventually find a new way to progress without needing to [[backtracking|backtrack]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theverge.com/2018/10/18/17995428/hitman-2-io-interactive-sven-liebold-interview-gigantic-levels-columbia-ghost-mode|title=How Hitman 2's developers turned its gigantic levels into ever-evolving playgrounds|first=Nick|last=Slatt|work=[[The Verge]]|date=October 19, 2018|accessdate=January 20, 2024|archive-date=20 October 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231020030248/https://www.theverge.com/2018/10/18/17995428/hitman-2-io-interactive-sven-liebold-interview-gigantic-levels-columbia-ghost-mode|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="making sapeniza"/> There are two types of levels in this game; "fortress" refers to an area the player must infiltrate, and a "snailhouse" is a level that has a circular design in which players are encouraged to explore the peripheral areas to find ways to access the area in the middle of the map.<ref name="simulation"/> The level Sapienza was developed alongside Paris and was designed as the "opposite" of it, both in level design layout and aesthetic. Inspired by Italy's [[Amalfi]] coast and the town of [[Vernazza]], the maps feature a ''snailhouse'' design. Elverdem described this level as the "pinnacle" of the Swiss cheese design because the map has a lot of verticality and the pathways are interconnected, ensuring players will not find a dead end.<ref name="making sapeniza">{{cite web|url=https://www.pcgamer.com/the-making-of-sapienza-hitmans-best-level/|title=The making of Sapienza, Hitman's best level|first=Phil|last=Savage|work=[[PC Gamer]]|date=3 January 2017|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200416004328/https://www.pcgamer.com/the-making-of-sapienza-hitmans-best-level/|archive-date=16 April 2020|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="RPS Hokkaido"/> According to designer Jesper Hylling, the team mainly did their location research remotely using [[Google Images]], [[YouTube]] and [[Google Street View]].<ref name="RPS Hokkaido">{{cite web|url=https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/2017/03/24/how-hitmans-hokkaido-level-was-made/|title=How Hitman's Hokkaido level was made|first=Alex|last=Wiltshire|work=[[Rock, Paper, Shotgun]]|date=24 March 2017|access-date=30 August 2020|archive-date=9 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200809123036/https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/2017/03/24/how-hitmans-hokkaido-level-was-made/|url-status=live}}</ref>

The team spent time into designing "believable everyday life" to ensure that players feel immersed in a level. According to the team, the team relied heavily on subtle [[environmental storytelling]]. For instance, IO's artists were instructed to write a short story for each hotel room in the Bangkok level, and tell the story using only "set dressings", how objects are placed in an environment, to indicate the personality or the circumstance of the room occupant.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/how-hitman-uses-thoughtful-level-design-to-tell-stories/|title=How 'Hitman' Uses Subtle Level Design to Tell Stories|first=Kevin|last=Wong|work=[[Vice (magazine)|Vice]]|date=December 2, 2016|access-date=January 20, 2024|archive-date=24 February 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240224004042/https://www.vice.com/en/article/pgkvmn/how-hitman-uses-thoughtful-level-design-to-tell-stories|url-status=live}}</ref> The team incorporated a concept known as "social stealth", in which players are expected to conform to [[social norm]]s and abide by the rules in a particular setting or context to blend in.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.gameinformer.com/games/hitman/b/pc/archive/2016/03/01/io-interactive-wants-you-to-hide-in-plain-sight.aspx|title=Hitman: IO Interactive Wants You To Hide In Plain Sight|first=Luke|last=Walaszek|magazine=[[Game Informer]]|date=1 March 2016|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190824162944/https://www.gameinformer.com/games/hitman/b/pc/archive/2016/03/01/io-interactive-wants-you-to-hide-in-plain-sight.aspx|archive-date=24 August 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> The team was inspired by sociology theories by [[Pierre Bourdieu]], who proposed that different social spaces carry different rules, and [[Erving Goffman]], who proposed that human behaviours will change depending on different social states and settings.<ref name="gamasutra">{{cite web|url=https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/mapping-out-the-subtle-social-cues-throughout-i-hitman-i-s-level-design|title=Mapping out the subtle social cues throughout Hitman's level design|first=Alissa|last=McAloon|work=[[Game Developer (magazine)|Game Developer]]|date=March 19, 2019|accessdate=January 20, 2024|archive-date=20 January 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240120120437/https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/mapping-out-the-subtle-social-cues-throughout-i-hitman-i-s-level-design|url-status=live}}</ref> Each area in a map is considered to be a [[microbiome]] that informs players the way they should act. At each level, the team balanced the proportion of public and private spaces. Players are able to freely walk around in public spaces without restrictions, which enables them to understand the "feel" of the level and discover mission opportunities, although there are certain public settings with implied social rules. The developers use these to teach players the basics of social stealth and the rules of trespassing without punishing players with gameplay penalties.<ref name="gdcpdf">{{cite web|url=https://ubm-twvideo01.s3.amazonaws.com/o1/vault/gdc2019/presentations/MettePodenphantAndersen_HitmanSocial.pdf|title=Hitman Levels as Social Spaces: The Social Anthropology of Level Design|first=Mette|last=Pødenphant Andersen|work=[[IO Interactive]]|accessdate=January 20, 2024|archive-date=2 October 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241002104910/https://ubm-twvideo01.s3.amazonaws.com/o1/vault/gdc2019/presentations/MettePodenphantAndersen_HitmanSocial.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref> There are two types of private spaces; professional spaces that often require a disguise and personal spaces in which the target can be alone.<ref name="murder space">{{cite web|url=https://www.pcgamer.com/how-the-creators-of-hitman-use-social-science-to-design-perfect-murder-playgrounds/|title=How the creators of Hitman use social science to design perfect murder playgrounds|first=Joseph|last=Knoop|work=[[PC Gamer]]|date=20 March 2019|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190403145855/https://www.pcgamer.com/how-the-creators-of-hitman-use-social-science-to-design-perfect-murder-playgrounds/|archive-date=3 April 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> Private areas usually have distinct art assets to contrast them with public spaces, rewarding player's exploration and curiosity.<ref name="murder space"/> The AI of targets displays two types of behaviour; some will roam around the map and others will station themselves in a private space that is off-limits to the player. This helped diversify the gameplay loop by encouraging different playstyles. According to the team, the first type of target encourages players to follow them and observe their behaviour and patterns while the latter type prompts players to find ways to infiltrate a setting or gain access to previously restricted areas.<ref name="simulation"/>

After receiving complaints about the level being lifeless and boring from playtesters, the team introduced narrative subplots into the game with mission stories and opportunities. These elements position the players on a "rail" that will guide them to their target; this added additional challenges to the game's simulation because opportunities will disrupt the target's usual loop and players can complicate the loop by abandoning an ongoing opportunity in favour of another rail. Despite this complication, the team believed these subplots allow players to discover creative ways that change the AI loop in a meaningful and organic manner. For instance, if the Ether virus is destroyed in Sapienza, one of the targets, scientist Francesca DeSantis, will deviate from her core loop to visit the laboratory. Players can easily use this feature to manipulate the targets. Despite putting players on a rail, the team stopped giving players further instructions after they have gathered all of the information needed to carry out the hit. The team felt it encourages players to decide how to approach the targets and communicates to the player there is never a "wrong" way of killing a target.<ref name="simulation"/>

Another result of the playtesting complaints was IO Interactive heavily expanding upon the tutorial missions set at the ICA Facility. The tutorial was designed to teach players the fundamentals of ''Hitman,'' how to operate the game and how to set their own goals. The first iteration was a series of individual test chambers where the player would be taught a single mechanic or feature at a time. However, even though this taught players how to operate the game, it was not representative of the nature of the game as an open sandbox. The redesigned tutorial consisted of a short 'Arrival' opening that teaches basic movement and camera controls, a 'Guided training' mission set on a sandbox yacht level and then an unguided 'Final Test' sandbox level. However, despite teaching the controls and the fundamentals of ''Hitman'', developers still felt they had to teach players how to set their own goals so this led to the idea of the 'Freeform training' mission. In this mission players are asked to replay the yacht level from the 'Guided training' again but this time without any guidance and with more items such as remote explosives available to play with. Playtesters were given a list of challenges on paper that were deliberately designed to be simple and to work well together. This resulted in players setting their own goals and becoming creative in trying to complete all the different challenges.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Level Design in Hitman: Guiding Players in a Non-Linear Sandbox |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hc8_W2PERZE |language=en |work=[[Game Developers Conference]] |date=February 21, 2019 |access-date=2022-06-07 |archive-date=7 June 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220607132257/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hc8_W2PERZE |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Story ===
Vogt and Elverdam placed more emphasis on the game's narrative because they observed the market wanted "quality drama" following the success of ''[[The Last of Us (video game)|The Last of Us]]'' (2013). Vogt noted there was a genre change for the franchise with ''Hitman'' (2016); unlike the previous games in the series, which are crime thrillers, the 2016 game is an "agent thriller" that was inspired by [[James Bond]] movies such as ''[[Casino Royale (2006 film)|Casino Royale]]'' and has a more "adventurous and aspirational" tone than the older games, which are "cold and cynical".<ref name="redesigning 47"/> The team elevated the stature of Agent 47 and his targets; 47 is now travelling to luxurious and exotic locations, and assassinating targets who are social elites and powerful criminals. Elverdem said with the genre change, Agent 47 became "the guy you called for the most impossible hits under the most impossible circumstances".<ref name="redesigning 47"/> To make the game aspirational, it has a "stronger moral compass"<ref name="redesigning 47"/> than earlier games in the series so the assassinations committed by Agent 47 are more morally justifiable and make more sense in the context of the in-game universe.<ref name="redesigning 47"/>

Vogt described Agent 47 as a "quintessential blank slate character"<ref name="redesigning 47"/> and Elverdam said "since he is not anyone himself, it's easy for him to be everyone else".<ref name="redesigning 47"/> Agent 47's only goal is to complete his assignments. Given the nature of the character, the team cannot forcefully apply typical character arcs like [[hero's journey]] for him; the team felt this would cause [[ludonarrative dissonance]]. The team introduced other characters to accompany Agent 47 through the post-2016 ''Hitman'' games. 47's handler Diana Burnwood becomes his conscience and the Shadow Client—who is revealed as Lucas Grey in ''[[Hitman 2 (2018 video game)|Hitman 2]]''—serves as his emotions. These characters have genuine emotions and desires, and their actions and attitudes would slowly influence Agent 47 and facilitate his own [[character arc]].<ref name="redesigning 47"/> [[David Bateson]] returned to voice Agent 47.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/will-the-real-agent-47-please-stand-up-855/|title=Talking to the Voice Behind the Hitman Games|first=Paul|last=Weedon|work=[[Vice (magazine)|Vice]]|date=13 October 2015|access-date=9 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190929015620/https://www.vice.com/en_au/article/bnp5xq/will-the-real-agent-47-please-stand-up-855|archive-date=29 September 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>

Vogt was initially concerned by the game's episodic format; he felt the episode would feel like "a slice of an unfinished game" if one episode features too many narrative elements.<ref name="redesigning 47"/> The team thus decided to include subplots within each level while the main story would slowly unfold throughout the games. This unfolding makes the game similar to a television series in which some episodes are entirely about a subplot that has no relation to the overarching narrative.<ref name="redesigning 47">{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Cf3bdBw99_Y|title=Redesigning Hitman's Agent 47|first=Danny|last=O'Dwyer|work=[[Noclip]]|via=[[YouTube]]|date=7 August 2019|access-date=7 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200523185424/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Cf3bdBw99_Y|archive-date=23 May 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> Vogt said Season 1 only serves to introduce the game's characters and that the game's story would become increasingly important in later seasons. The first half of Season 1 has very little story content because the team wanted to ensure players can relate themselves to Agent 47, a merciless assassin who travels around the world to kill targets assigned to him.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gamespot.com/articles/hitmans-story-is-just-getting-started-at-the-end-o/1100-6444238/|title=Hitman's Story Is "Just Getting Started" At the End of Season 1, Writer Says|first=Mat|last=Paget|work=[[GameSpot]]|date=6 October 2016|access-date=6 October 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161008160900/http://www.gamespot.com/articles/hitmans-story-is-just-getting-started-at-the-end-o/1100-6444238/|archive-date=8 October 2016|url-status=live}}</ref> Because Agent 47 is a blank state character, the team strove to create a "living, breathing" world.<ref name="living breathing"/> Rather than a protagonist, Agent 47 is an intruder who observes and occasionally interrupts other people's lives. To achieve this, the team relied heavily on environmental storytelling. Art director Jonathan Rowe said the art team spent a lot of time "set dressing" every room and item to ensure each item has a reason to be there and has a tale to tell. For instance, some rooms in the Bangkok hotel are messy, communicating the story of the previous inhabitants of these rooms.<ref name="living breathing">{{cite web|url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/how-hitman-uses-thoughtful-level-design-to-tell-stories/|title=How 'Hitman' Uses Thoughtful Level Design to Tell Stories|first=Kevin|last=Wong|work=[[Vice (magazine)|Vice]]|date=2 December 2016|access-date=7 June 2020|archive-date=22 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200922183852/https://www.vice.com/en_us/article/pgkvmn/how-hitman-uses-thoughtful-level-design-to-tell-stories|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Online ===
''Hitman'' is always online due to the inclusion of Elusive Targets who can only be killed once. The making of Elusive Targets did not impact the game's level design; the team used a different design philosophy compared with the main game. Players are not allowed to replay Elusive Targets because the team felt this would create a tense experience and prevent players from noticing imperfections that would make the experience less enjoyable.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pcgamesn.com/hitman/hitman-elusive-targets-second-try|title=Hitman's Elusive Targets will never be re-released because "they wouldn't stand up"|first=Joel|last=Gregory|work=[[PCGamesN]]|date=7 September 2016|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180616130417/https://www.pcgamesn.com/hitman/hitman-elusive-targets-second-try|archive-date=16 June 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> Elusive Targets were designed to be memorable; they do not always have connections to the main story, which gave the team more freedom to create characters that fit the setting and theme of each map. The team avoided releasing Elusive Targets in a newly released map; they wanted to give sufficient time for players to master and explore the level. The development team observed the ways players completed Elusive Targets, their play patterns and feedback, and made adjustments to make future targets more challenging.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/designing-the-elusive-targets-system-in-2016-s-i-hitman-i-|title=Designing the Elusive Targets system in 2016's Hitman|first=Torben|last=Ellert|work=[[Gamasutra]]|date=4 October 2016|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200606043005/https://www.gamasutra.com/view/news/282601/Designing_the_Elusive_Targets_system_in_2016s_Hitman.php|archive-date=6 June 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> Hannes Seifert, the head of IO Interactive, described Elusive Targets as "the pulse" of the experience that has "energised" the community and boosted the game's sales.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/articles/2016-11-07-io-interactive-is-chasing-the-most-elusive-target-of-all|title=IO Interactive is chasing the most elusive target of all|first=Matthew|last=Handrahan|work=[[Gameindustry.biz]]|date=7 November 2016|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200316151357/https://www.gamesindustry.biz/articles/2016-11-07-io-interactive-is-chasing-the-most-elusive-target-of-all|archive-date=16 March 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> This mode was intended to provide bursts of content to the player during intervals between episodes. In July 2016, a companion app that allows players to keep track of online content released for the game was released.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2016/07/07/hitman-has-a-new-app-and-his-6th-elusive-target-has-a-twin|title=Hitman Has a New App, and His 6th Elusive Target Has a Twin|first=Matt|last=Porter|work=[[IGN]]|date=7 July 2016|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170923024428/http://www.ign.com/articles/2016/07/07/hitman-has-a-new-app-and-his-6th-elusive-target-has-a-twin|archive-date=23 September 2017|url-status=live}}</ref>

In March 2016, advertising company Omelet announced they had collaborated with Square Enix for a new campaign called "Choose Your Hit". Players could vote online and through [[Twitter]] to "kill" either [[Gary Cole]] or [[Gary Busey]]; the actor who received the most votes would lend his voice and likeness to the target in an upcoming mission. A month later, it was announced Busey had won and would appear as the target in a mission that would be released in mid-2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gamespot.com/articles/hitman-promo-asks-you-to-kill-gary-busey-or-gary-c/1100-6435924/|title=Hitman Promo Asks You to Kill Gary Busey or Gary Cole|first=Mat|last=Paget|work=[[GameSpot]]|date=22 March 2016|access-date=13 April 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160412035552/http://www.gamespot.com/articles/hitman-promo-asks-you-to-kill-gary-busey-or-gary-c/1100-6435924/|archive-date=12 April 2016|url-status=live}}</ref> On 18 July 2016, Busey was announced as the seventh elusive target in the game; his mission, in which Cole also appears, would be available for seven days starting on 21 July 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hitman.com/en-gb/news/elusive-target-7|title=Elusive Target #7|access-date=18 July 2016|date=18 July 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160815232903/https://hitman.com/en-gb/news/elusive-target-7|archive-date=15 August 2016|url-status=live}}</ref>

A mode called Contracts mode, which first appeared in ''Absolution'', was added to ''Hitman''. The team believed the larger maps with more NPCs in each make the experience more varied and created identifiable NPCs to make these custom targets more interesting.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamereactor.eu/ios-hannes-seifert-on-hitmans-swiss-cheese-game-design/|title=IO's Hannes Seifert on Hitman's "Swiss cheese game design"|first=Mike|last=Holmes|work=[[Gamereactor]]|date=10 February 2016|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-date=2 October 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241002105022/https://www.gamereactor.eu/ios-hannes-seifert-on-hitmans-swiss-cheese-game-design/|url-status=live}}</ref> When ''Absolution'' launched in 2012, the online servers were unstable due to a large number of players accessing the online Contracts mode; to avoid a repeat of this incident and to ensure ''Hitman'' had a stable launch, IO Interactive improved the game's online infrastructure.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/hitman-interview-why-were-going-episodic/1100-6434429/|title=Hitman Interview: Why We're Going Episodic|first=Alexa Ray |last=Corriea|work=[[GameSpot]]|date=10 February 2016|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170822053109/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/hitman-interview-why-were-going-episodic/1100-6434429/|archive-date=22 August 2017|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Release ==
[[Square Enix]], [[IO Interactive]]'s parent company, published the episodes throughout 2016 as well as the downloadable and retail version ''Hitman: The Complete First Season''. ''The Complete First Season,'' which bundles all of the game's episodes, was released on 31 January 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/hitman-the-complete-first-seasons-disc-release-lau/1100-6443180/|title=Hitman: The Complete First Season's Disc Release Launches in January|first=Tamoor|last=Hussain|work=[[GameSpot]]|date=31 August 2016|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190702214532/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/hitman-the-complete-first-seasons-disc-release-lau/1100-6443180/|archive-date=2 July 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Feral Interactive]] released the ''Definitive Edition'' on [[Linux]] and [[macOS]] on 16 February and 20 June 2017 respectively.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamasutra.com/view/pressreleases/300080/Enter_a_World_of_Assassination_in_HITMAN.php|title=Enter a World of Assassination in HITMAN|work=[[Gamasutra]]|date=15 June 2017|access-date=30 August 2020|archive-date=6 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210206183751/https://www.gamasutra.com/view/pressreleases/300080/Enter_a_World_of_Assassination_in_HITMAN.php|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pcgamesn.com/hitman/hitman-linux|title=Hitman – The Complete First Season is releasing on Linux on 16 February|work=[[PCGamesN]]|first=Kirk|last=McKeand|date=7 February 2017|access-date=30 August 2020|archive-date=24 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201024144328/https://www.pcgamesn.com/hitman/hitman-linux|url-status=live}}</ref> Because of the game's poorer-than-expected financial performance and Square Enix prioritisation of other properties, Square Enix announced in June 2017 to divest IO Interactive and allow the studio's management to [[management buyout|buy it out]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mcvuk.com/io-interactive-becomes-an-independent-studio-retains-hitman-ip/ |title=IO Interactive becomes an independent studio, retains Hitman IP |first=Sean |last=Cleaver |date=16 June 2017 |website=[[MCV (magazine)|MCV]] |access-date=22 September 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190922203518/https://www.mcvuk.com/io-interactive-becomes-an-independent-studio-retains-hitman-ip/ |archive-date=22 September 2019 |url-status=live}}</ref>

''Hitman'' was originally set to be released on 8 December 2015 for [[PlayStation 4]], [[Windows]], and [[Xbox One]], but its release was postponed to 11 March 2016 to allow time for IO Interactive to include more content in the base game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.videogamer.com/ps4/hitman/news/hitman_delayed_to_march_2016.html|title=Hitman delayed to March 2016|first=David|last=Scammell|work=VideoGamer.com|date=23 September 2015|access-date=23 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304083448/http://www.videogamer.com/ps4/hitman/news/hitman_delayed_to_march_2016.html|archive-date=4 March 2016|url-status=live}}</ref> The PlayStation 4 version of the game includes six exclusive missions known as ''The Sarajevo Six''. Players who pre-ordered the game gained access to its [[Software release life cycle#Beta|beta]], which was released for PlayStation 4 on 12 February and for Windows on 19 February 2016.<ref name="prequel">{{cite web|url=http://www.vg247.com/2015/12/05/heres-a-few-details-about-the-hitman-beta-coming-in-february/|title=Here's a few details about the Hitman beta coming in February|date=5 December 2015|access-date=7 December 2015|first=Stephany|last=Nunneley|work=[[VG247]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170810153654/https://www.vg247.com/2015/12/05/heres-a-few-details-about-the-hitman-beta-coming-in-february/|archive-date=10 August 2017|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2015-06-16-new-hitman-has-playstation-exclusive-beta-for-those-who-pre-order|title=New Hitman has PlayStation 4-exclusive beta for those who pre-order|work=[[Eurogamer]]|first=Wesley|last=Yin-Poole|date=16 June 2015|access-date=16 June 2015|archive-date=2 October 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241002105028/https://www.eurogamer.net/new-hitman-has-playstation-exclusive-beta-for-those-who-pre-order|url-status=live}}</ref> No [[Season pass (video gaming)|season pass]] was available at launch; the company considered the addition of paid content a "wrong approach".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://venturebeat.com/2015/06/18/hitman-wont-have-a-season-pass-we-think-its-wrong/|title=Hitman won't have a season pass: 'We think it's wrong'|first=Dan|last=Crawley|work=[[VentureBeat]]|date=18 June 2015|access-date=21 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150623214012/http://venturebeat.com/2015/06/18/hitman-wont-have-a-season-pass-we-think-its-wrong/|archive-date=23 June 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> Players who pre-ordered the game also received a costume pack based on a mission from ''Blood Money'' and two in-game weapons.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pcgamer.com/hitman-system-requirements-and-preorder-bonus-revealed/|title=Hitman system requirements and preorder bonus revealed|first=Andy|last=Chalk|work=[[PC Gamer]]|date=9 February 2016|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181212150555/https://www.pcgamer.com/hitman-system-requirements-and-preorder-bonus-revealed/|archive-date=12 December 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> A beta was released prior to the game's official launch.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pcgamer.com/hitman-beta-details-accompany-new-trailer/|title=Hitman beta details accompany new trailer|first=Angus|last=Morrison|work=[[PC Gamer]]|date=8 February 2016|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170630094654/http://www.pcgamer.com/hitman-beta-details-accompany-new-trailer/|archive-date=30 June 2017|url-status=live}}</ref>

Following the buyout, independent IO Interactive retained the rights to the ''Hitman'' franchise and began self-publishing the game digitally with the released "ICA Facility", the game's prologue, as a [[free-to-play]] game in June 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.polygon.com/2017/6/20/15838230/hitman-prologue-free-download-pc-ps4-xboxone|title=Hitman's prologue is now free to play|first=Thomas|last=Biery|work=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]|date=20 June 2020|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190330203824/https://www.polygon.com/2017/6/20/15838230/hitman-prologue-free-download-pc-ps4-xboxone|archive-date=30 March 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> IO Interactive then released ''Hitman: Game of the Year Edition'' on 7 November 2017 for download; the re-release includes the base game and a separate campaign named "Patient Zero", a remix of the Bangkok, Sapienza, Colorado, and Hokkaido episodes.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/hitman-goty-edition-adds-a-4-mission-campaign-and-murder-clown-challenges-in-november/|title=Hitman: GOTY Edition adds a 4-mission campaign and murder clown challenges in November|first=Connor|last=Sheridan|work=[[GamesRadar]]|date=24 October 2017|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180212091808/http://www.gamesradar.com/hitman-goty-edition-adds-a-4-mission-campaign-and-murder-clown-challenges-in-november/|archive-date=12 February 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> It also includes a new costume inspired by ''Blood Money'', and new music composed by Niels Bye Nielsen.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pushsquare.com/news/2017/10/hitman_game_of_the_year_edition_adds_new_campaign_and_content|title=Hitman: Game of the Year Edition Adds New Campaign and Content|first=Sammy|last=Barker|work=[[Push Square]]|date=October 24, 2017|access-date=October 12, 2020|archive-date=21 May 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220521165221/https://www.pushsquare.com/news/2017/10/hitman_game_of_the_year_edition_adds_new_campaign_and_content|url-status=live}}</ref> In April 2018, IO Interactive announced to partner with [[Warner Bros. Interactive Entertainment]] to release the ''Game of the Year Edition'' for retail on 15 May 2018. The edition, which is titled ''Hitman: Definitive Edition'', includes the campaign and the bonus episodes, as well as the "IO Interactive's 20th Anniversary Outfit Bundle", which includes outfits inspired by IO's other franchises such as ''[[Freedom Fighters (video game)|Freedom Fighters]]'', ''[[Mini Ninjas]]'', and ''[[Kane & Lynch]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.polygon.com/2018/4/4/17197174/hitman-definitive-edition-release-date-io-interactive-warner-bros|title=Hitman getting new 'Definitive Edition,' thanks to Warner Bros.|first=Michael|last=McWhertor|work=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]|date=4 April 2018|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612135919/https://www.polygon.com/2018/4/4/17197174/hitman-definitive-edition-release-date-io-interactive-warner-bros|archive-date=12 June 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>

IO Interactive released the ''Game of the Year Edition'' on the [[GOG.com]] digital storefront on 22 September 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |date=22 September 2021 |title=Release: HITMAN - Game of The Year Edition |url=https://www.gog.com/news/release_hitman_game_of_the_year_edition |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220905211346/https://www.gog.com/news/release_hitman_game_of_the_year_edition |archive-date=5 September 2022 |access-date=2022-04-18 |website=GOG.com |language=en-US}}</ref> This release received significant backlash online and large amounts of negative user reviews on the game's store page due to the always-online requirements of the game which was felt to go against GOG's stated "[[Digital rights management|DRM]]-free games" character. At that time, GOG stated in a forum post stating that users were free to refund the game but warned against "[[review bombing]]". They later clarified that they would only remove reviews that go against their review guidelines after pushback from forum users about the suggestion their complaints were "review bombing".<ref>{{Cite news |first=Jody |last=MacGregor |date=2021-09-25 |title=GOG users aren't happy about Hitman's online requirements |language=en |work=PC Gamer |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/uk/gog-users-arent-happy-about-hitmans-online-requirements/ |access-date=2022-04-18 |archive-date=28 October 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211028052010/https://www.pcgamer.com/uk/gog-users-arent-happy-about-hitmans-online-requirements/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The game was removed from the store on 9 October, with GOG writing in a statement "we shouldn't have released it [''Hitman''] in its current form".<ref>{{Cite news |date=2021-10-09 |title=GOG pulls Hitman from its own store, admits it shouldn't have released it in its current form |language=en-gb |work=Eurogamer.net |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/gog-pulls-hitman-from-its-own-store-admits-it-shouldnt-have-released-it-in-its-current-form |access-date=2022-04-18 |archive-date=2 October 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241002105025/https://www.eurogamer.net/gog-pulls-hitman-from-its-own-store-admits-it-shouldnt-have-released-it-in-its-current-form |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Release format ===
While there was no post-launch support for ''Absolution'', the team realised players regularly re-visited the game's Contracts mode, in which players set custom targets and share them online with other players. This mode's longevity encouraged IO Interactive to re-evaluate the release model of ''Hitman'', which they envisioned as a "[[game as a service|digital platform]]" that is similar to a [[Netflix]] series. This platform, which was marketed as the "World of Assassination", allowed IO Interactive to regularly release content without rebuilding the technology. The team believed launching the game at a lower price point with fewer levels would encourage more players to purchase it, creating positive [[word of mouth]] that would expand the game's player base. As the team released more episodes, the expected new players would convert their existing version to the full version. The team initially estimated about 80% of the purchasers would buy the episodes separately while the other 20% of them, whom they believed to be long-time fans of the series, would purchase the full-priced versions.<ref name="Hitman Rise and fall"/>

Originally, the game was to be released in an "intro pack" that would include all of the base content and locations, six-story missions, three sandboxes, forty "signature kills", a contracts mode with 800 targets, and access to regular events held by the developer. New missions and locations set in Thailand, the US, and Japan were to be released after the game's launch, and a full-priced version was to be released following the release of this post-release content.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.polygon.com/2015/9/29/9414265/hitman-2016-release-date-intro-pack-content|title=New Hitman coming 11 March 2016—here's what's in the game at launch|first=Michael|last=McWhertor|work=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]|date=29 September 2015|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161217042932/http://www.polygon.com/2015/9/29/9414265/hitman-2016-release-date-intro-pack-content|archive-date=17 December 2016|url-status=live}}</ref> No [[downloadable content]] (DLC) was to be released for the game and no [[microtransactions]] were to be offered; new missions, locations, and targets were to be regularly added to the game as free post-release updates.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.engadget.com/2015/06/16/new-episodic-hitman/|title=The new 'Hitman' will be an 'ever-expanding world of assassination'|first=Joseph|last=Volpe|work=[[Engadget]]|date=16 June 2015|access-date=21 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150620030000/http://www.engadget.com/2015/06/16/new-episodic-hitman/|archive-date=20 June 2015|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pcgamer.com/hitman-release-date-announced-will-expand-over-time/|title=Hitman release date announced|first=Phil|last=Savage|work=[[PC Gamer]]|date=16 June 2015|access-date=16 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150618160348/http://www.pcgamer.com/hitman-release-date-announced-will-expand-over-time/|archive-date=18 June 2015|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 14 January 2016, it was announced ''Hitman'' would be released in an [[Episodic video game|episodic]] manner; at its launch, the game would consist of the prologue and Paris missions. New content would be released monthly; this would include the remaining two cities of the main game (Sapienza and Marrakesh) in April and May 2016 respectively, which would be followed by the previously planned Thailand, US, and Japan expansions in late 2016. Weekly events would be held and additional content would be released between the monthly updates. These expansions would be available at no extra cost to purchasers of a full-priced, downloaded copy of the game but purchasers of the "Intro Pack" would buy this extra content separately. According to Seifert, the move was designed to allow the team time to develop the game's levels and to "create a living game that will expand and evolve over time and establish a foundation for the future—this is the first game in a storyline which will continue and expand with future ''Hitman'' games".<ref name=polygon-episodic>{{cite news|title=Hitman changes release structure again, now 'fully episodic'|url=http://www.polygon.com/2016/1/14/10770628/hitman-dlc-fully-episodic|access-date=14 January 2016|work=Polygon|agency=Vox Media|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160114203020/http://www.polygon.com/2016/1/14/10770628/hitman-dlc-fully-episodic|archive-date=14 January 2016|url-status=live}}</ref>

The episodic release enabled IO Interactive to receive feedback for earlier levels and fix some of the design flaws during the production of later episodes.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2016-11-01-it-was-a-good-spot-we-ended-up-in-but-it-was-messy-getting-there|title=It was a good spot we ended up in. But it was messy getting there|first=Martin|last=Robinson|work=[[Eurogamer]]|date=1 November 2016|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171120153304/http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2016-11-01-it-was-a-good-spot-we-ended-up-in-but-it-was-messy-getting-there|archive-date=20 November 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> The positive reaction to Sapienza boosted the team's confidence and encouraged them to continue experimenting with level design by modifying the design principles in later maps, which add new challenges and change players' expectations.<ref name="Sapeniza map">{{cite web|url=https://www.pcgamer.com/the-making-of-sapienza-hitmans-best-level/|title=The making of Sapienza, Hitman's best level|first=Phil|last=Savage|work=[[PC Gamer]]|date=3 January 2017|access-date=7 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200416004328/https://www.pcgamer.com/the-making-of-sapienza-hitmans-best-level/|archive-date=16 April 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> The team also believed by periodically releasing episodes, players would be encouraged to replay and master each level, and share their experience with other players while awaiting the next episode.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mashable.com/2017/01/12/hitman-season-1-christian-elverdam-interview/|title=2016's 'Hitman' was great because it didn't let players binge|first=Adam|last=Rosenberg|work=[[Mashable]]|date=12 January 2017|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200121041749/https://mashable.com/2017/01/12/hitman-season-1-christian-elverdam-interview/|archive-date=21 January 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Episodes ===
In addition to the ICA Facility level, which serves as the prologue and a tutorial to the game, ''Hitman'' features six locations, including [[Paris]], France; the fictional town of [[Sapienza (Hitman)|Sapienza]], Italy; [[Marrakesh]], Morocco; [[Bangkok]], Thailand; [[Colorado]], United States; and [[Hokkaido]], Japan.

After the release of Marrakesh, IO Interactive announced a "Summer Bonus Episode" that was released on 19 July 2016 and features a remake of the Sapienza and Marrakesh levels, new targets, challenges and opportunities. Additionally, there are several additional "bonus" episodes for 47 to complete.
* "The Icon":<ref name="summer_bonus">{{cite web|url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/hitman-summer-bonus-episode-detailed-requires-seas/1100-6441931/|title=Hitman Summer Bonus Episode Detailed, Requires Season Pass to Play Today|first=Tamoor|last=Hussain|work=[[GameSpot]]|date=19 July 2016|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190103092526/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/hitman-summer-bonus-episode-detailed-requires-seas/1100-6441931/|archive-date=3 January 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> 47 is given a contract to assassinate actor-director Dino Bosco on the set of his new superhero movie to save L'Avventura Pictures from being driven into bankruptcy by Bosco's incompetence and the film's over-inflated budget.
* "A House Built on Sand":<ref name="summer_bonus" /> Prior to the events of "A Gilded Cage", 47 is hired to assassinate Matthieu Mendola, chief architect of international contractor Hamilton-Lowe, and Kong Tuo-Kwang, CEO of rival firm China Corp., who had hired Mendola to steal valuable trade secrets. 47 kills both men and recovers the stolen goods for the client.
* "Holiday Hoarders":<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hitman.com/news/hitman-holiday-content#|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220073816/https://hitman.com/news/hitman-holiday-content|url-status=dead|archive-date=20 December 2016|title=Hitman|website=Hitman}}</ref> 47 takes on an assignment to eliminate professional thieves Harry Bagnato and Marv Gonif, both on the run from American authorities, as they attempt to rob the Palais De Walewska during a [[Christmas]] celebration. The targets are a nod to [[Joe Pesci]]'s and [[Daniel Stern (actor)|Daniel Stern]]'s characters from the holiday film ''[[Home Alone]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.polygon.com/2016/12/13/13942176/hitman-home-alone-burglars-holiday-hoarders-dlc|title=Hitman's latest target: The two burglars from Home Alone|first=Owen S.|last=Good|work=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]|date=13 December 2016|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190804153651/https://www.polygon.com/2016/12/13/13942176/hitman-home-alone-burglars-holiday-hoarders-dlc|archive-date=4 August 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>
* "Landslide": Prior to the events of "World of Tomorrow", 47 is hired by Silvio Caruso to assassinate Marco Abiatti, a wealthy businessman and right-wing politician with mafia ties who is running for mayor of Sapienza with the intention of demolishing most of the town so he can build expensive luxury resorts on the land.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pcgamer.com/hitmans-landslide-bonus-mission-out-next-week-19th-elusive-target-revealed/|title=Hitman's Landslide bonus mission out next week, 19th elusive target revealed|first=Joe|last=Donnelly|work=[[PC Gamer]]|date=27 January 2017|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180119142533/http://www.pcgamer.com/hitmans-landslide-bonus-mission-out-next-week-19th-elusive-target-revealed/|archive-date=19 January 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>
