''Hitman'' received generally positive reviews according to [[review aggregator]] [[Metacritic]]. Many reviewers regarded the game as a "return to form" for the series after the controversial release of ''Absolution'' in 2012.<ref name="return to form"/><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/gaming/what-to-play/hitman-review-a-devilishly-delightful-return-to-form/|title=Hitman review: 'a devilishly delightful return to form'|first=Sam|last=White|newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]]|date=14 March 2016|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190429050154/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/gaming/what-to-play/hitman-review-a-devilishly-delightful-return-to-form/|archive-date=29 April 2019|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/new-hitman-confident-return-classic-form/|title=The new Hitman is a confident return to classic form|first=Leon|last=Hurley|work=[[GamesRadar]]|date=10 February 2016|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200330164912/https://www.gamesradar.com/new-hitman-confident-return-classic-form/|archive-date=30 March 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

Many reviewers expressed skepticism at the game's release schedule. When the Paris episode was launched, Arthur Gies of ''[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]'' said the game was more unfinished than episodic.<ref>{{cite web |last=Gies |first=Arthur |date=10 March 2016 |url=http://www.polygon.com/2016/3/10/11195428/hitman-review |title=Hitman review |publisher=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]] |access-date=10 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160311024327/http://www.polygon.com/2016/3/10/11195428/hitman-review |archive-date=11 March 2016 |url-status=live }}</ref> Phil Savage from ''[[PC Gamer]]'' said, "''Hitman'' feels unrefined and unfinished in lots of small but important ways".<ref>{{cite web |last=Savage |first=Phil |date=14 March 2016 |url=http://www.pcgamer.com/hitman-intro-pack-review/ |title=Hitman: Intro Pack review |publisher=[[PC Gamer]] |access-date=14 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160315113442/http://www.pcgamer.com/hitman-intro-pack-review/ |archive-date=15 March 2016 |url-status=live }}</ref> As more episodes were released, critics' impressions of the release format improved significantly. Mike Williams from ''[[USgamer]]'' said the episodic release format helped increase the replayability of ''Hitman'' because it gave sufficient time for the players to fully explore a level and experiment with different approaches before a new episode was released.<ref name="USgamerRev">{{cite web|url=https://www.usgamer.net/articles/hitman-season-one-pc-review-physical-release|title=Hitman Season One PC Review: The Best Damned James Bond Game You'll Ever Play|first=Mike|last=Williams|work=[[USgamer]]|date=5 June 2019|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191008135839/https://www.usgamer.net/articles/hitman-season-one-pc-review-physical-release|archive-date=8 October 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> Reviewers from ''[[Rock, Paper, Shotgun]]'' said the episodic release model meant the game would not be overwhelming for players, that it "[set] an excellent precedent for having impeccable chunks once a month", and that other games should be inspired by this release structure.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/2017/02/03/hitman-season-one-review-pc/|title=Hitman Season One: RPS discusses favourite levels and what we want from season two|first=Alec|last=Meer|website=[[Rock Paper Shotgun]]|date=3 February 2017|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200529093741/https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/2017/02/03/hitman-season-one-review-pc/|archive-date=29 May 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> According to the developers, the format would encourage players to regularly return to and replay each level.<ref name="VentureBeat episodic">{{cite web|url=https://venturebeat.com/2017/03/10/hitman-is-a-living-sandbox-not-an-episodic-game/|title=Hitman is a living sandbox, not an episodic game|first=Jeff|last=Grubb|work=[[VentureBeat]]|date=10 March 2017|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190614212614/https://venturebeat.com/2017/03/10/hitman-is-a-living-sandbox-not-an-episodic-game/|archive-date=14 June 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>

The locations received praise from critics. Williams liked the vast and lively levels, which he described as "playgrounds" players can freely explore and observe.<ref name="USgamerRev"/> Savage also said the levels are "intricate" and "dense", meaning players would have plenty to do in each level, encouraging them to replay the game.<ref name="PCGRev">{{cite web|url=https://www.pcgamer.com/hitman-the-complete-first-season-review/|title=Hitman: The Complete First Season review|first=Phil|last=Savage|work=[[PC Gamer]]|date=31 January 2017|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191224150250/https://www.pcgamer.com/hitman-the-complete-first-season-review/|archive-date=24 December 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> He also liked the variety of the levels presented, especially later levels, which he said add new challenges to the game. ''[[GameSpot]]''{{'}}s Brett Todd also admired the complex design of each level and commented, "the levels are so big and so packed with details that they take on lives of their own, much like separate movies in a franchise".<ref name="GSpotRev">{{cite web|url=https://www.gamespot.com/reviews/hitman-review/1900-6416576/|title=Hitman review|first=Brett|last=Todd|work=[[GameSpot]]|date=23 November 2016|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200606153205/https://www.gamespot.com/reviews/hitman-review/1900-6416576/|archive-date=6 June 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> Writing for ''[[Game Informer]]'', Jeff Marchiafava said the levels are too big and that players could not stumble upon meaningful opportunities in an organic and spontaneous manner. He also said a lot of [[trial and error]] was needed for later episodes because the rules had changed, resulting in a lot of frustration.<ref name="GIRev">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.gameinformer.com/games/hitman_season_1/b/playstation4/archive/2017/01/31/hitman-season-1-review-game-informer.aspx|title=Hitman Season 1: The Complete Package Still Comes Up Short|first=Jeff|last=Marchiafava|magazine=[[Game Informer]]|date=31 January 2017|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190823224426/https://www.gameinformer.com/games/hitman_season_1/b/playstation4/archive/2016/11/15/hitman-season-1-review-game-informer.aspx|archive-date=23 August 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> ''[[Eurogamer]]''{{'}}s Edwin Evans-Thirlwell was disappointed the AI did not react sufficiently to the players' actions.<ref name="EuroGRev">{{cite web|url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2017-01-31-hitman-the-complete-first-season-review|title=Hitman: The Complete First Season review|first=Edwin|last=Evans-Thirlwell|date=11 May 2017|access-date=8 June 2020|work=[[Eurogamer]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200418044943/https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2017-01-31-hitman-the-complete-first-season-review|archive-date=18 April 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> 

Critics generally agreed Paris was a promising start to the series, though Sapienza was often named as the game's high point due to the map's complex layout, location variety, and creative assassinations. Marrakesh and Hokkaido were released to a generally positive reception but Bangkok and Colorado were considered to be weaker levels because the assassinations are less creative and the art style is less striking. The Colorado level was often considered to be controversial among players due to its complete lack of public spaces and verticality.<ref name="EuroGRev"/><ref name="USgamerRev"/> Critics liked the idea of a global-trotting adventure; Williams and Todd drew similarities between ''Hitman'' and the James Bond films.<ref name="GSpotRev"/><ref name="USgamerRev"/> Some reviewers expressed disappointment that the game reuses voice actors in different locations.<ref name="GSpotRev"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/hitman-the-complete-first-season-review-vast-environments-filled-with-possibilities-and-potential/|title=Hitman: The Complete First Season review|first=Phil|last=Savage|work=[[GamesRadar]]|access-date=8 June 2020|date=30 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200207063834/https://www.gamesradar.com/hitman-the-complete-first-season-review-vast-environments-filled-with-possibilities-and-potential/|archive-date=7 February 2020|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="GIRev"/>

The gameplay received critical praise. Williams said players are able to experiment with different ways to assassinate their targets. As the player progresses, they unlock new tools, which allow them to discover new assassination opportunities, further boosting the game's [[replay value]].<ref name="USgamerRev"/> Andy Kelly from ''PC Gamer'' said, "if you have an absurd idea, the game will almost always accommodate and react to it".<ref name="return to form">{{cite web|url=https://www.pcgamer.com/the-new-hitman-is-a-brilliant-return-to-form/|title=The new Hitman is a brilliant return to form|first=Andy|last=Kelly|work=[[PC Gamer]]|date=27 December 2016|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191214194549/https://www.pcgamer.com/the-new-hitman-is-a-brilliant-return-to-form/|archive-date=14 December 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> Savage said the opportunities are "entertaining" because they often result in very creative assassinations. Todd said the assassinations feel like "more of a funhouse ride than a grim series of contract killings" due to the game's over-the-top nature.<ref name="GSpotRev"/> Jeffrey Matulef from ''[[Eurogamer]]'' also commented on AI behaviour, which generates many unscripted moments for players.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2017-01-20-the-funniest-game-ive-played-is-about-murder|title=The killing joke: How Hitman turns murder into farce|first=Jeffery|last=Matulef|work=[[Eurogamer]]|date=20 January 2017|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180203084446/http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2017-01-20-the-funniest-game-ive-played-is-about-murder|archive-date=3 February 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> Some reviewers said the opportunities are too overbearing because the game offers players too much guidance and hand-holding.<ref name="EuroGRev"/> Reviewers praised IO Interactive for allowing players to play with minimal hints by modifying the game's settings.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.polygon.com/2016/3/10/11195428/hitman-review|title=Hitman review|first=Arthur|last=Gies|work=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]|date=10 March 2016|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191008135902/https://www.polygon.com/2016/3/10/11195428/hitman-review|archive-date=8 October 2019|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="USgamerRev"/> Many reviewers said the game feels like a puzzle game because of the way the player deciphers AI patterns and approaches their objectives.<ref name="PCGRev"/><ref name="USgamerRev"/> Savage said the game has the "most elegant implementation" of the disguise system because it introduces a specific type of NPC that will recognise 47's disguise rather than [[Hitman: Blood Money|''Blood Money''{{'}}s]] "arbitrary suspicion meter",<ref name="PCGRev"/> though several reviewers said the pattern remained difficult to discern.<ref name="GSpotRev"/><ref name="GIRev"/> Several critics also disliked the game's always-online requirement and its long [[load time]]s.<ref name="GIRev"/><ref name="GSpotRev"/>

=== Sales ===
Contrary to the developers' expectations, ''Hitman''{{'s}} episodic format did not succeed commercially. Most of the players purchased the full-priced versions and the sales volume was significantly lower than the traditional boxed release. Due to market confusion over the game's episodic format, even when the game's development was completed, the retail version did not meet publisher Square Enix's expectations, causing it to divest from the studio.<ref name="simulation"/> ''Hitman: The Complete First Season'' was the fourth-best-selling video game at retail in the UK during its week of release, behind ''[[Resident Evil 7: Biohazard]]'' (2017), ''[[Grand Theft Auto V]]'' (2013), and ''[[FIFA 17]]'' (2016).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.videogamer.com/news/resident-evil-7-holds-at-no1-for-a-second-week|title=Resident Evil 7 holds at No.1 for a second week|first=James|last=Orry|work=VideoGamer.com|date=6 February 2017|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170617204916/https://www.videogamer.com/news/resident-evil-7-holds-at-no1-for-a-second-week|archive-date=17 June 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> Despite the slow start, IO Interactive announced the game had attracted seven million players as of November 2017 and more than 13 million players had played the game by May 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.destructoid.com/hitman-has-passed-13-million-players-504583.phtml|title=Hitman has passed 13 million players|first=Jordan|last=Devore|work=[[Destructoid]]|date=25 May 2018|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200330074348/https://www.destructoid.com/hitman-has-passed-13-million-players-504583.phtml|archive-date=30 March 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Accolades ===
''Hitman'' was nominated for Best Action/Adventure Game at [[The Game Awards 2016]] and Evolving Game at the [[13th British Academy Games Awards]].<ref name=":0">{{cite web| url=http://www.gamespot.com/articles/all-the-2016-game-awards-nominees/1100-6445481/| title=All the 2016 Game Awards Nominees| first=Eddie| last=Makuch| date=16 November 2016| access-date=18 November 2016| work=[[GameSpot]]| url-status=live| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170118191246/http://www.gamespot.com/articles/all-the-2016-game-awards-nominees/1100-6445481/| archive-date=18 January 2017| df=mdy-all}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{cite web|url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2017/04/07/bafta-games-awards-2017-winners-revealed|title=BAFTA Game Awards 2017 Winners Revealed|first=Joe|last=Skrebels|work=[[IGN]]|date=7 April 2017|access-date=28 April 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170420130044/http://www.ign.com/articles/2017/04/07/bafta-games-awards-2017-winners-revealed|archive-date=20 April 2017}}</ref> Video game publication ''[[Giant Bomb]]'' named ''Hitman'' their [[List of Game of the Year awards|Game of the Year]] in 2016; the staff said, "2016 was filled with huge debuts, finales, and resurrections, but the surprise success of ''Hitman'' had us talking, sweating, cursing, and laughing more than any other game this year".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.giantbomb.com/articles/giant-bombs-2016-game-of-the-year-awards-day-five/1100-5525/|title=Giant Bomb's 2016 Game of the Year Awards: Day Five|work=[[Giant Bomb]]|date=30 December 2016|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200510225140/https://www.giantbomb.com/articles/giant-bombs-2016-game-of-the-year-awards-day-five/1100-5525/|archive-date=10 May 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Legacy ==
===''World of Assassination'' trilogy ===
A sequel titled ''[[Hitman 2 (2018 video game)|Hitman 2]]'' was released by Warner Bros. Interactive Entertainment in November 2018 for PlayStation 4, Windows, and Xbox One.<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Khan |first=Imran |date=7 June 2018 |title=Hitman 2 Revealed, Coming November |url=https://www.gameinformer.com/2018/06/07/hitman-2-revealed-coming-november |url-status=live |magazine=[[Game Informer]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612162056/https://www.gameinformer.com/2018/06/07/hitman-2-revealed-coming-november |archive-date=12 June 2018 |access-date=8 June 2018}}</ref> "Hitman: Legacy Pack" was released on 9 November 2018 as DLC for ''Hitman 2''; all of the missions from the first season of the game were made available in the new game with the improved [[game mechanics]] used in ''Hitman 2''.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Romano |first1=Sal |date=20 August 2018 |title=Hitman 2 DLC 'Hitman Legacy Pack' announced, includes all six locations from Season 1 |url=https://www.gematsu.com/2018/08/hitman-2-dlc-hitman-legacy-pack-announced-includes-all-six-locations-from-season-1 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191216124821/https://gematsu.com/2018/08/hitman-2-dlc-hitman-legacy-pack-announced-includes-all-six-locations-from-season-1 |archive-date=16 December 2019 |access-date=9 April 2020 |website=Gematsu}}</ref> IO Interactive developed and published another sequel, ''[[Hitman 3]],'' which was released in January 2021, and concludes the story arc started in ''Hitman''.<ref>{{cite web |last=Chalk |first=Andy |date=12 June 2020 |title=Hitman 3 is coming in January |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/hitman-3-is-coming-in-january/ |access-date=12 June 2020 |work=[[PC Gamer]] |archive-date=11 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200611220258/https://www.pcgamer.com/hitman-3-is-coming-in-january/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

A digital-only collection of all the games from the ''World of Assassination'' trilogy was released on 20 January 2022. It features ''Hitman 3'' as well as access passes to play the content from ''Hitman 2'' and ''Hitman'' inside ''Hitman 3.'' A ''Premium Add-Ons'' bundle includes all DLC for the games, excluding the "Seven Deadly Sins" DLC from ''Hitman 3''. The ''Hitman Trilogy'' bundle can be found on the PS4 and PS5, Xbox Series X/S, Steam and The [[Epic Games Store]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Moore |first=Jared |date=2022-01-13 |title=Hitman Trilogy Is Coming Next Week, and It's On Xbox Game Pass |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/hitman-trilogy-coming-next-week-xbox-game-pass |access-date=2022-12-06 |website=IGN |language=en |archive-date=5 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230305222811/https://www.ign.com/articles/hitman-trilogy-coming-next-week-xbox-game-pass |url-status=live }}</ref> ''Hitman 3'' was rebranded as ''Hitman: World of Assassination'' on January 26, 2023, with all content from the previous two games imported to ''Hitman 3'' free of charge. This made the game available on [[Google Stadia|Stadia]] and the original ''Hitman'' was delisted from sales.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/hitman-3-being-rebranded-as-world-of-assassination-putting-entire-trilogy-in-one-package|title=Hitman 3 Being Rebranded as World of Assassination, Putting Entire Trilogy in One Package|first=Ryan|last=Dinsdale|work=[[IGN]]|date=January 5, 2023|accessdate=August 2, 2023|archive-date=31 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230731175429/https://www.ign.com/articles/hitman-3-being-rebranded-as-world-of-assassination-putting-entire-trilogy-in-one-package|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Other media===
IO Interactive partnered with [[Dynamite Entertainment]] to create ''Agent 47: Birth of the Hitman'', a six-issue comic book miniseries that ran from November 2017 to June 2018, and was later released as a graphic novel in 2019.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Barbour |first1=Travis |date=11 September 2017 |title=HITMAN Comic Book Announcement |work=IO Interactive |url=https://www.ioi.dk/hitman-comic-book-announcement/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170915104447/https://www.ioi.dk/hitman-comic-book-announcement/ |archive-date=15 September 2017 |access-date=8 June 2020 |publisher=[[IO Interactive]]}}</ref> The series ties-in with the ''World of Assassination'' trilogy and depicts 47's life before the events of the games, including his upbringing at Dr. Ort-Meyer's asylum and his previous career as a brainwashed assassin for Providence alongside his best friend, Lucas Grey / Subject 6. IO Interactive had complete control over the storyline of the comic.

In November 2017, [[Hulu]] and [[Fox 21 Television Studios]] announced they would produce a television series based on the game. [[Derek Kolstad]], Adrian Askarieh and [[Chuck Gordon]] would also serve as its executive producers.The pilot episode would be written by Kolstad.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/hitman-tv-series-from-john-wick-writer-derek-kolst/1100-6454899/|title=Hitman TV Series From John Wick Writer Derek Kolstad In The Works At Hulu|first=Chris E|last=Hayner|work=[[GameSpot]]|date=14 November 2017|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190713123536/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/hitman-tv-series-from-john-wick-writer-derek-kolst/1100-6454899/|archive-date=13 July 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> Kolstad has stated that his adaption of Agent 47 will differ slightly from that of the vision IO has already made. Despite being announced in 2017, he doesn't know when the TV series will start filming.<ref>{{cite web |last=Kazmanko |first=Vlad |date=25 March 2021 |title=Agent 47 will have hair in the upcoming hitman tv show |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2015/09/09/agent-47-will-have-hair-in-the-upcoming-hitman-tv-series |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210325000000/https://www.ign.com/articles/2015/09/09/agent-47-will-have-hair-in-the-upcoming-hitman-tv-series |archive-date=25 March 2021 |access-date=25 March 2021 |work=[[TheGamer]] }} [https://www.thegamer.com/agent-47-will-keep-his-hair-in-the-upcoming-hitman-tv-series/ Alt URL] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230128033043/https://www.thegamer.com/agent-47-will-keep-his-hair-in-the-upcoming-hitman-tv-series/ |date=28 January 2023 }}</ref>
